findings.topic: C/Fitting a 7-inch HMI (181x108x15 mm board) into a modular board door
findings.claim: In 4x18 boards (depth 97-108 mm) the module front faces sit nearly flush with the cover plate and the door is only ~8-15 mm in front, so a 15 mm-thick 181x108 mm display board cannot sit in the door without leaving one row empty and cutting the cover plate; a transparent plastic door (Golf, Practibox) is thin and not suited to a 160x90 mm cut-out; only metal-door 150-170 mm deep boards (Hager univers FW, PrismaSeT XS) or Eaton BP-O (262 mm) can take it, still sacrificing one row (board spans ~10 modules x 1 row).
findings.detail: Engineering assessment from listed depths; modular devices are ~70 mm deep, DIN rail to front cover ~45 mm; row pitch 125-150 mm; board 181x108 mm, active 153.8x85.6 mm.

findings.topic: HMI/How installers mount a 7-inch HMI in a steel door
findings.claim: Industrial 7-inch HMIs use a rectangular cut-out of about 192x138 mm (some 186x128) and are clamped from behind with 4-6 mounting clips at 0.5-0.6 Nm; accepted panel thickness 1.0-5 mm (steel 1.5-6 mm); the HMI's own front gasket restores IP65 at the door. For bare ESP32 boards there is no industrial bezel kit: practice is a cut-out slightly smaller than the glass (~156x88 mm for 153.8x85.6 active area, or ~165x100 mm to show the whole glass), M3 standoffs on the 3.2 mm PCB holes into the door, and a 3D-printed/laser-cut bezel with foam gasket (ready models exist on Printables/Thingiverse/MakerWorld); 'ramka montazowa 7 cali' on Allegro returns only RPi desk cases (33-100+ zl), not panel-mount frames.
findings.detail: Cut-out 192x138 mm (7.6x5.4 in) for generic 7-inch HMI protective cover 220x180x24 mm; Beijer X2 pro 7: clips, 0.5-0.6 Nm, panel 1.0-5.0 mm; Phoenix HMI wall mounting kit 2701380 exists; Waveshare RPi5 7-inch case 32316 and 11301 case on Allegro; VESA is irrelevant for door mounting.

findings.topic: Size reference table (outer HxWxD, plate, weight)
findings.claim: Consolidated: 800x600x250 - Eaton CS-86/250 plate 770x550x3, 32.7 kg; Legrand 036931 plate ~737x543, 30.9 kg; S3D 8625P 27.8 kg; ETI GT 80-60-25 30.1 kg; Adelid OM806025 26.7 kg; Rittal AE 1058.500 34 kg / AX 1058.000 32 kg. 1000x600x300 - Eaton CS-106/300 plate 970x550x3, 44.8-45.4 kg; ETI GT 100-60-30 39.8 kg; CRN 106300P 38.2 kg. 1000x800x300 - Rittal AX 1180.000 plate 745x975x2.5, 52 kg; Adelid OM1008030 ~48.6 kg (shipping).
findings.detail: 700x500x250 and 600x400x250: Eaton CS-75/250, CS-64/250 exist (CS-75/200 archived Allegro 14195915641; CS-55/250 Allegro 8055718606; CS-66/250 Allegro 12726003849); ETI GT 70-50-25 and GT 60-40-25 (001102121) exist, Allegro price not captured.

recommendations: Primary choice: steel wall enclosure 1000x800x300 with full mounting plate - Rittal AX 1180.000 on Allegro (1582 zl, IK10, 2.5 mm plate 745x975, two gland plates, 52 kg) or Adelid OM1008030 (1649 zl) if Rittal stock/shipping fails. This size gives ~745x975 mm of plate for 4 TH35 rows (incl. Shelly Pro DIN units, fault relays/contactors, DIN meter), 60-80 mm ducts, CT space on supply wires, and keeps natural-convection rise to ~14 K at 150 W.

Compact alternative if wall space is limited: 800x600x300 (Eaton CS-86/300 ~935-1000 zl or Adelid OM806030 899 zl). Prefer 300 mm depth over 250 mm: door-mounted 7-inch board (15 mm + standoffs) plus 70 mm DIN devices plus 20-30 mm plate/duct clearance consumes ~130 mm, leaving margin for wiring behind the door only at 300 mm.

Do not use a modular 4x18/6x24 distribution board as the main enclosure: depths 97-168 mm, IP30/40, plastic transparent doors, and no room for a 15 mm display in the door without sacrificing a row; use one only as a sub-panel for MCB/RCD presentation if the client wants a 'typical home board' look.

Avoid plastic (ABS/polyester) for this unit: lower heat conduction (~1.6x higher temperature rise), no bonded metal body for PE-fault demonstrations, and branded sizes (Fibox ARCA 806030, PLM86G) cost 1600-3500 zl without plate; generic ABS 600x400x200 at ~250 zl is too small.

HMI: mount the ESP32-8048S070 (181x108 mm) directly in the steel door - cut ~165x100 mm (whole glass) or ~156x88 mm (active area) opening, fix with M3 standoffs on the 3.2 mm PCB holes, add a 3D-printed bezel with closed-cell foam gasket; keep the opening on the hinge-far half of the door and route the display cable with a flexible loom. If an industrial look is wanted, use a standard 192x138 mm cut-out and a commercial 7-inch HMI instead.

Thermal: at <=150 W the 1000x800x300 steel box needs no fan (dT ~14 K); if 'burnt/loose contact' heaters push dissipation to 200 W or ambient >30 C, add a 150x150 or 204x204 filter fan (ATV2200 58 m3/h 203 zl / ATV3200 308 zl) low on one side, a 223x223 ClimaSys outlet grille (166 zl) high on the opposite side, and a KTS 011 thermostat (22-40 zl); accept IP54.

DIN layout: TH35x15 perforated rails (2 m, 13-28 zl) bolted to the plate on 10-20 mm stand-offs where cable ducts cross; ~125-150 mm row pitch; reserve the bottom 150 mm above the gland plate for terminals, CTs on the 6 mm2 feeders and the DLB CT leads.

Ask for the client's enclosure sign-off on: size (800x600x300 vs 1000x800x300), brand tier (Adelid vs Rittal/Eaton), hinge side, door-mounted HMI yes/no, and whether a transparent door matters (only Legrand factory glazed or Eaton accessory door offer it; none on Allegro).
open_questions_for_user: Which Shelly models are in stock (Shelly Pro 1/2/3/4PM/3EM are DIN-rail 1-2 module units; Plus/Gen3 are flush-box modules needing adapters) - this sets the DIN-module count and therefore the enclosure size.
Will the board be wall-mounted permanently or moved to demos/trainings? A 1000x800x300 steel box weighs 50-60 kg empty; 800x600x300 is 30-35 kg.
Indoor only (IP40 would suffice) or also outdoor/van transport (keep IP54-66)?
Is a transparent/glazed door required to show the wiring (adds 500-2000 zl and limits brands), or is a plain steel door with the 7-inch HMI acceptable?
How much heat will the 'burnt contact' / high-resistance simulation dump continuously (resistor wattage)? Above ~150 W a filter fan is needed.
Should the HMI sit in the door or in a separate small desk/console box connected by cable (safer for a 230/400 V demo door that will be opened often)?
